unit.title: Fractions as Parts of a Whole

contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you compared fractions with the same denominator. Today: fractions that look different but are actually equal!

Equivalent fractions name the same amount even though the numbers are different. 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent — half a pizza is the same amount whether you cut it into 2 slices and take 1, or cut it into 4 slices and take 2. Draw two identical rectangles: divide one into 2 equal parts and shade 1, divide the other into 4 equal parts and shade 2. Do the shaded areas look the same size?
You just discovered equivalent fractions — different numbers, same amount! Tomorrow we'll review everything from this week.

objectives: Understand that equivalent fractions represent the same amount with different numerators and denominators
Verify 1/2 = 2/4 by drawing and comparing shaded areas in identical shapes
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's fraction-comparison work.
2. Introduce equivalent fractions using the pizza example.
3. Have the child draw and shade the two rectangles to verify 1/2 = 2/4.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use the exact same physical object (like a paper strip) folded two different ways, rather than two separately-drawn shapes
Ready for more: ask the child to find a third fraction equivalent to 1/2 (like 3/6) by drawing a shape with 6 equal parts
This is a foundational idea for later grades' fraction work — a solid visual understanding now matters more than symbolic shortcuts
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1/2 and 2/4 are equivalent — both shaded areas cover exactly half of the identical rectangles.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 3 standard 3.NF.3a-b: recognizing and generating simple equivalent fractions, completing this week's fractions thread before tomorrow's review.
